intro: Welcome to cleft sentences! Today you learn to put a spotlight on the most important part of a sentence: What I need is more time. It was Sari who called. All I want is some peace. You already do this in Indonesian with 'yang' and '-lah', so you'll see the bridge quickly.
teachingNotes: A cleft sentence splits one simple sentence into two parts so that one part gets the focus (Indonesian: satu kalimat dibelah dua supaya satu bagian mendapat sorotan). Bridges to Indonesian: What I need is… ≈ Yang saya butuhkan adalah…; It was Sari who called ≈ Sari-lah yang menelepon; All I want is… ≈ Yang saya mau cuma…. Recap in one line from B1/B2 relative clauses: who for people, which for things, that for both; in it-clefts use who or that for a person and that for everything else. In speech the focused part carries the main stress (It was SARI who called; What I need is more TIME).

What-clefts: What + clause + is/was + focus (What I need is more time; What worries me is the deadline). What happened was (that) the server crashed. Do-pseudo-cleft for an action: What we did was (to) call the client: base verb, 'to' optional. The verb after the what-clause is normally singular: What we need is more staff. Some speakers say 'What we need are new laptops' before a plural noun; is is always safe, so don't test is vs are before a plural noun. Tense: is for now, was for the past. Common error 1: *What I need it is more time: Indonesian 'adalah' becomes is, but there is no extra it. Also *That I need is… / *The thing what… (what only at the start, that after the thing).

It-clefts: It + is/was + focus + who/that + the rest (It was Sari who called; It was in 2021 that we moved; It's the delivery time that worries me). Use them to correct a misunderstanding or contrast: It wasn't Budi who called, it was Sari; It's not the price that worries me, it's the delivery time. Always It is/It was, even for plural focus (It was Sari and Budi who…). Common error 2: *It was Sari she called me, from 'Sari-lah yang': yang becomes who/that, never she. Keep who/that; don't drop it. For time and place, that is the safe choice; when/where are heard in informal speech, so accept them but teach that.

All / the thing / the reason / the place clefts: All I want is some peace (all = the only thing, Indonesian 'cuma'); The thing that worries me is the deadline; The reason (why) I called is (that)…; The place where we met was a café in Bandung; The person who helped me most was Bu Ani. Common error 3: *All what I want is… → All I want / All that I want (Indonesian 'semua yang' pushes learners to 'all what'). 'The reason I called is because…' is very common in speech but criticised in formal writing; 'The reason … is that…' is the safe choice: say so, don't test it.

Style, honestly: clefts are not more correct, they change the focus. Only test clear cases: grammar errors (it is, she, all what, wrong verb form after What we did was), or a short exchange where the context decides which part must be in focus. Typed answers are normalised (punctuation removed). Scope: no inversion (Never have I…), no emphatic do (I do like it), no reversed clefts as a topic (More time is what I need: recognise only), no subjunctive or nominalisation. If asked, say they come in other lessons.

keyPoints.title: What-clefts: What I need is…
keyPoints.explanation: Start with What + a short clause, then is/was, then the part you want to highlight at the end: What I need is more time. What worries me is the deadline. For an action, use What … did was + base verb: What we did was call the client. Use is (not are) as the safe choice, and never add it: 'What I need it is' is wrong.

Untuk tindakan, pakai What … did was + kata kerja dasar: What we did was call the client. Pakai is (bukan are) sebagai pilihan aman, dan jangan tambahkan it: 'What I need it is' salah.

keyPoints.title: It-clefts: It was Sari who called
keyPoints.explanation: It is/It was + the part in focus + who/that + the rest. Use who or that for a person, that for a thing, a time or a place: It was Sari who called. It was in 2021 that we moved. It-clefts are great for correcting a misunderstanding: It's not the price that worries me, it's the delivery time. Indonesian 'Sari-lah yang' → It was Sari who (not 'Sari she').

keyPoints.title: All I want is… / The thing that worries me is…
keyPoints.explanation: All + clause + is = 'the only thing' (Indonesian 'cuma'): All I want is some peace. Not 'All what I want': say All I want or All that I want. The same pattern works with the thing, the reason, the place and the person: The thing that worries me is the deadline. The reason I called is that the invoice is wrong. The place where we met was a café in Bandung.

Pola yang sama bisa dipakai dengan the thing, the reason, the place dan the person: The thing that worries me is the deadline. The reason I called is that the invoice is wrong. blocks.text:
**Cleft** means *split in two*. A **cleft sentence** takes one simple sentence and splits it into two parts so that **one part gets the spotlight**.
Simple: *Sari called.* Cleft: *It was **Sari** who called.* The meaning is the same, but now the listener knows that **Sari** (not Budi, not Rina) is the important information.
You already do this in Indonesian:
- *Yang saya butuhkan adalah lebih banyak waktu* → ***What** I need **is** more time.*
- *Sari**-lah yang** menelepon* → ***It was** Sari **who** called.*
- *Yang saya mau **cuma** ketenangan* → ***All** I want **is** some peace.*
Quick recap from your relative-clause lessons: **who** for people, **which** for things, **that** for both. In clefts you'll mostly use **who** and **that**.
In speech, the part in focus gets the **strongest stress**: *It was **SA**ri who called. What I need is more **TIME**.*

id.text:
**Cleft** artinya *terbelah dua*. **Cleft sentence** mengambil satu kalimat sederhana lalu membelahnya menjadi dua bagian supaya **satu bagian mendapat sorotan**.
Kalimat biasa: *Sari called.* Cleft: *It was **Sari** who called.* Artinya sama, tapi sekarang pendengar tahu bahwa **Sari** (bukan Budi, bukan Rina) adalah informasi pentingnya.
Kamu sebenarnya sudah melakukan ini dalam bahasa Indonesia:
- *Yang saya butuhkan adalah lebih banyak waktu* → ***What** I need **is** more time.*
- *Sari**-lah yang** menelepon* → ***It was** Sari **who** called.*
- *Yang saya mau **cuma** ketenangan* → ***All** I want **is** some peace.*
Pengingat singkat dari pelajaran relative clause: **who** untuk orang, **which** untuk benda, **that** untuk keduanya. Di cleft, kamu paling sering memakai **who** dan **that**.
Saat bicara, bagian yang disorot mendapat **tekanan suara paling kuat**: *It was **SA**ri who called. What I need is more **TIME**.*

blocks.text: **Honest note on style:** a cleft is not 'more correct' than a simple sentence. It just moves the spotlight. Use it when you want to **correct someone**, **contrast** two things, or build up to the important point. Too many clefts in one text sound dramatic, so use them where the focus really matters.

id.text: **Catatan jujur soal gaya:** cleft tidak 'lebih benar' daripada kalimat biasa. Cleft hanya memindahkan sorotan. Pakai saat kamu ingin **meluruskan** orang lain, **membandingkan** dua hal, atau membangun ke poin pentingnya. Terlalu banyak cleft dalam satu teks terdengar dramatis, jadi pakai di tempat yang fokusnya benar-benar penting.

blocks.prompt: In 'It was Pak Hasan who signed the contract', which part gets the spotlight?
blocks.explain: In an it-cleft, the part right after It was is the focus: Pak Hasan (Pak Hasan-lah yang menandatangani), not someone else.

id.prompt: Dalam 'It was Pak Hasan who signed the contract', bagian mana yang mendapat sorotan?

blocks.text:
**Pattern:** ***What** + a short clause + **is/was** + the focus.* (A **clause** = a part of a sentence with its own subject and verb, like *I need* or *worries me*.)
- *What I need **is** more time.* (Yang saya butuhkan adalah…)
- *What worries me **is** the deadline.* (Yang membuat saya khawatir adalah…)
- *What happened **was** (that) the server crashed during the demo.* (Yang terjadi adalah…)
Here **what** is not a question. It means *the thing that* (hal yang / yang).
**For an action**, use **do**: *What we **did** was **call** the client.* After *was* use the **base verb** (*call*, not *called*), with or without *to*: *What we did was **to call** the client* is also correct.
**is or was?** Present clause → **is**; past clause → **was**: *What I wanted **was** a window seat.*
**Singular verb:** after a what-clause, **is** is the normal, safe choice, even before a plural noun: *What we need **is** more staff.* (You may hear *What we need are new laptops*; that's fine in speech, but *is* is never wrong.)

id.text:
**Pola:** ***What** + bagian kalimat pendek + **is/was** + fokusnya.* (**Clause** = bagian kalimat yang punya subjek dan kata kerja sendiri, misalnya *I need* atau *worries me*.)
- *What I need **is** more time.* (Yang saya butuhkan adalah…)
- *What worries me **is** the deadline.* (Yang membuat saya khawatir adalah…)
- *What happened **was** (that) the server crashed during the demo.* (Yang terjadi adalah…)
Di sini **what** bukan pertanyaan. Artinya *hal yang* (yang).
**Untuk tindakan**, pakai **do**: *What we **did** was **call** the client.* Setelah *was* pakai **kata kerja dasar** (*call*, bukan *called*), boleh dengan atau tanpa *to*: *What we did was **to call** the client* juga benar.
**is atau was?** Bagian kalimat masa kini → **is**; masa lalu → **was**: *What I wanted **was** a window seat.*
**Kata kerja tunggal:** setelah what-clause, **is** adalah pilihan biasa yang aman, bahkan sebelum kata benda jamak: *What we need **is** more staff.* (Kamu mungkin mendengar *What we need are new laptops*; itu wajar saat bicara, tapi *is* tidak pernah salah.)

material.title: It-clefts: It was Sari who called

blocks.text:
**Pattern:** ***It is / It was** + the focus + **who/that** + the rest.*
- A **person** in focus → **who** or **that**: *It was **Sari who** called.*
- A **thing** → **that**: *It's **the delivery time that** worries me.*
- A **time** or **place** → **that**: *It was **in 2021 that** we moved. It was **in Bandung that** they met.* (In casual speech you'll also hear *when* and *where*; **that** is the safe choice.)
Use **It is** for now and **It was** for the past. It stays **It was** even when the focus is plural: *It was **Sari and Budi** who organised the event* (not *'They were Sari and Budi'*).
**The best use: correcting a misunderstanding.** Put the wrong idea with **not**, then the right one:
- *It wasn't Budi who called, **it was Sari**.*
- *It's **not** the price that worries me, **it's** the delivery time.*

id.text:
**Pola:** ***It is / It was** + fokusnya + **who/that** + sisanya.*
- **Orang** yang disorot → **who** atau **that**: *It was **Sari who** called.*
- **Benda** → **that**: *It's **the delivery time that** worries me.*
- **Waktu** atau **tempat** → **that**: *It was **in 2021 that** we moved. It was **in Bandung that** they met.* (Dalam obrolan santai kamu juga akan mendengar *when* dan *where*; **that** adalah pilihan aman.)
Pakai **It is** untuk sekarang dan **It was** untuk masa lalu. Tetap **It was** walaupun fokusnya jamak: *It was **Sari and Budi** who organised the event* (bukan *'They were Sari and Budi'*).
**Kegunaan terbaiknya: meluruskan salah paham.** Sebut ide yang salah dengan **not**, lalu yang benar:
- *It wasn't Budi who called, **it was Sari**.*
- *It's **not** the price that worries me, **it's** the delivery time.*

material.title: All I want is… / The thing that… / The reason…

blocks.text:
These work like what-clefts, but the first word adds meaning:
- **All** = *the only thing* (cuma): *All I want is some peace.* *All we did was ask a question.*
- **The thing that** = *the specific thing*: *The thing that worries me is the deadline.*
- **The reason (why)**: *The reason I called is that the invoice is wrong.* Or with **to**: *The reason I called was to ask about the invoice.*
- **The place (where)**: *The place where we met was a small café in Bandung.*
- **The person who**: *The person who helped me most was Bu Ani.*
**Watch out:** after **all**, never use **what**. Say *All I want* or *All that I want*, not *'All what I want'*. After **the thing**, use **that** (or nothing): *The thing (that) I like most…*, not *'The thing what…'*.

id.text:
Pola ini bekerja seperti what-cleft, tapi kata pertamanya menambah arti:
- **All** = *satu-satunya hal* (cuma): *All I want is some peace.* *All we did was ask a question.*
- **The thing that** = *hal yang spesifik*: *The thing that worries me is the deadline.*
- **The reason (why)**: *The reason I called is that the invoice is wrong.* Atau dengan **to**: *The reason I called was to ask about the invoice.*
- **The place (where)**: *The place where we met was a small café in Bandung.*
- **The person who**: *The person who helped me most was Bu Ani.*
**Hati-hati:** setelah **all**, jangan pakai **what**. Katakan *All I want* atau *All that I want*, bukan *'All what I want'*. Setelah **the thing**, pakai **that** (atau tanpa kata): *The thing (that) I like most…*, bukan *'The thing what…'*.

blocks.text:
**Indonesian trap:** *semua **yang** saya mau* pushes you towards *'all what I want'*. In English, **all** is followed directly by the clause: ***All I want** is…* (or *All **that** I want is…*).
**Style note:** *The reason I called is **because**…* is very common in speech, but some readers see it as repetitive. In formal writing, *The reason … is **that**…* is the safe choice.

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *semua **yang** saya mau* mendorongmu menulis *'all what I want'*. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **all** langsung diikuti bagian kalimatnya: ***All I want** is…* (atau *All **that** I want is…*).
**Catatan gaya:** *The reason I called is **because**…* sangat umum saat bicara, tapi sebagian pembaca menganggapnya berulang. Dalam tulisan formal, *The reason … is **that**…* adalah pilihan aman.

options: All what the client asked for was a short summary.
All the client asked for was a short summary.
All the client asked for it was a short summary.
blocks.explain: All + clause + was + focus. After all, don't add what, and don't add an extra it before was.

id.explain: All + bagian kalimat + was + fokus. Setelah all, jangan tambahkan what, dan jangan tambahkan it sebelum was.

id.title: All I want is… / The thing that… / The reason…

suggestedQuestions: When should I use an it-cleft instead of a what-cleft?
Why is it 'What we need is more staff' and not 'are'?
Can I say 'It was in 2021 when we moved'?
Which word do I stress in a cleft sentence?

resources.title: Emphasis: cleft sentences, inversion and auxiliaries
resources.note: A C1 page on it-clefts and what-clefts with two short gap-fill tests. It also covers inversion and emphatic do, which come in other lessons, and it doesn't cover all/the thing clefts.

id.note: Halaman C1 tentang it-cleft dan what-cleft dengan dua tes isian singkat. Halaman ini juga membahas inversion dan do untuk penekanan, yang ada di pelajaran lain, dan tidak membahas cleft dengan all/the thing.

resources.title: Grammar: Giving emphasis in English - BBC English Masterclass
resources.note: A short video on it-clefts: Sian uses It was … that to correct what someone misunderstood, focusing on a person, a thing or a time.

id.note: Video singkat tentang it-cleft: Sian memakai It was … that untuk meluruskan salah paham, dengan fokus pada orang, benda atau waktu.

resources.title: Grammar: Using 'what' to give emphasis - BBC English Masterclass
resources.note: A short video on what-clefts: the same holiday story told twice, first with normal sentences and then with What … is/was for emphasis.

id.note: Video singkat tentang what-cleft: cerita liburan yang sama diceritakan dua kali, pertama dengan kalimat biasa, lalu dengan What … is/was untuk penekanan.

flashcards.front: Yang saya butuhkan adalah lebih banyak waktu.
flashcards.back: What I need is more time. (no extra it)
It was Sari who called. (not 'Sari she')

flashcards.front: Yang membuat saya khawatir bukan harganya, tapi waktu pengirimannya.
flashcards.back: It's not the price that worries me, it's the delivery time.

flashcards.front: Yang kami lakukan adalah langsung menelepon klien.
flashcards.back: What we did was call the client straight away. (base verb)

flashcards.front: Yang saya mau cuma sedikit ketenangan.
flashcards.back: All I want is some peace and quiet. (not 'all what')

flashcards.front: Hal yang membuat saya khawatir adalah tenggat waktunya.
flashcards.back: The thing that worries me is the deadline.

flashcards.front: Alasan saya menelepon adalah tagihannya salah.
flashcards.back: The reason I called is that the invoice is wrong.

id.intro: Selamat datang di pelajaran cleft sentence! Hari ini kamu belajar menyorot bagian terpenting dari sebuah kalimat: What I need is more time. It was Sari who called. All I want is some peace. Dalam bahasa Indonesia kamu sudah melakukan ini dengan 'yang' dan '-lah', jadi kamu akan cepat melihat jembatannya.
suggestedQuestions: Kapan sebaiknya aku pakai it-cleft, bukan what-cleft?
Kenapa 'What we need is more staff' dan bukan 'are'?
Boleh nggak bilang 'It was in 2021 when we moved'?
Kata mana yang ditekan dalam cleft sentence?

assessment.clf-1: Lengkapi dengan satu kata: What the team needs right now ___ more time, not more meetings.
assessment.clf-2:
Tulis ulang kalimat ini supaya 'the traffic' mendapat sorotan. Mulai dengan kata-kata yang diberikan.
The traffic made us late for the meeting.
What made us late for the meeting …
assessment.clf-3:
Lengkapi dengan satu kata.
Dimas: Did Budi book the hotel for the Bali trip?
Rina: No, it was Sari ___ booked it. Budi booked the flights.
assessment.clf-4:
Tulis ulang kalimat ini supaya tahunnya mendapat sorotan. Mulai dengan kata-kata yang diberikan.
We moved our head office to Jakarta in 2018.
It was in 2018 …
assessment.clf-5:
Lengkapi dengan satu kata.
Bu Ani: So the new software is the problem?
You: No, it's ___ the software that's slowing us down, it's the internet connection.
assessment.clf-6:
Lengkapi dengan satu kata yang berarti 'satu-satunya hal'.
I don't need a big party for my birthday. ___ I want is a quiet dinner with my family.
assessment.clf-7:
Tulis ulang kalimat ini supaya 'the noise' mendapat sorotan. Mulai dengan kata-kata yang diberikan.
The noise from the construction site bothers me.
The thing that bothers me …
